what: The score is the fixed position's exact insertion-distance increase minus the candidate's depot distance. It is a generalized sequential-insertion criterion and takes O(1) time and memory per call. It uses only the supplied distance matrix and handles route boundaries, including an empty route.
why: Pure insertion cost can favor easy near-depot customers too early, even though construction deliberately seeds each route with a farthest customer. The depot-distance credit instead gives distant customers some urgency while the insertion term still strongly favors customers geometrically compatible with the current route. This tends to build coherent outer routes before returning toward the depot, a useful pattern for both clustered and radially spread layouts, and leaves 2-opt relatively compact routes to improve. The rule is intentionally inexpensive and scale-consistent, but it does not model demand packing, future insertions, or unassigned-customer density, and it offers no guarantee of improvement on every instance.
